context_requirements: DNA-PK catalytic activity is largely dispensable for basal transcription; a transcriptional response requires concurrent DNA damage (e.g., from irradiation or topoisomerase II poisons), which is absent in this experiment.
Any p21/CDKN1A suppression reported with DNA-PK inhibitors is seen only when p53 is activated by DNA damage; without damage, wild-type p53 lines show no change.
Cell lines with defective DNA-PK (e.g., V3) would be insensitive, but the nine lines here are DNA-PK-proficient and still require damage to reveal an effect.
falsifiers: A reproducible, dose-dependent change in the 978 landmark genes at 6 h or 24 h after 10 micromolar DNA-PK inhibitor alone in any of the nine cell lines.
Consistent suppression of CDKN1A (p21) or other p53 targets without a DNA-damaging co-treatment.
Induction of a DNA damage response signature (e.g., CDKN1A, GADD45A, MDM2, RPA2, TP53BP1) by the inhibitor alone.
Cell-cycle or apoptosis gene expression changes at 24 h in the absence of exogenous DNA damage.

evidence.supports: NU7441 potentiates ionizing radiation and etoposide cytotoxicity and retards DSB repair; effects require DNA damage.
NU7026 alone had no effect on cell cycle distribution; it potentiated topoisomerase II poisons.
OK-1035 suppressed p21 induction only after adriamycin-induced DNA damage, not by itself.
NU7441 alone did not prevent p53/p21 up-regulation; combination with radiation increased H2A.X phosphorylation and apoptosis.
NU7026 effects on checkpoint kinase-2, p53, H2A.X and G2 arrest were observed only in combination with ionizing radiation.
